extracted.intended_audience: attorneys who practice or seek to practice before the USPTO, OED staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order implementing 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state-court disbarment; it describes procedural notice, the grounds cited, the sanctions (exclusion, probation, possible additional suspension), and administrative steps (publication, restitution, notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40-day deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 was mailed by certified mail and provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice mailed by certified mail (receipt no. provided); delivery to Respondent triggers the forty-day window to respond; Respondent failed to file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), and reciprocal discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order determined (1) no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and (2) that exclusion from practice before the USPTO is appropriate because Respondent failed to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose reciprocal discipline (statutory/regulatory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statutory authority when imposing or announcing disciplinary actions involving practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the US PTO effective the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion applies to non-patent practice; note that the respondent is not a registered patent practitioner and is not authorized to practice patent law before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation upon reinstatement (two-year probationary period)
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when Respondent is reinstated to practice before the Office, Respondent shall be placed on probation for a period of two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation conditions include potential OED enforcement steps if the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director authority and Order to Show Cause procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply during probation, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order immediate suspension for up to sixty months, send the Order to Respondent at the last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the fifteen-day response period, if the OED Director remains of that opinion, the Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (a) the Order to Show Cause, (b) Respondent's response to it, if any, and (c) argument and evidence, and request immediate suspension up to sixty months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct the OED Director to publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette describing the respondent, the exclusion, and the grounds (violation citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should identify the respondent, state that the exclusion is for violating specific regulations (here 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)), summarize the state-court action, and cite statutory/regulatory authority for the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution as ordered by the state court
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall pay restitution as set forth in the Order of the Supreme Court of Arizona filed April 20, 2009.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO order may adopt or direct enforcement of restitution terms imposed by the state disciplinary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs the OED Director to give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the contact information and known admissions to notify relevant authorities and courts of USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide public access by posting disciplinary decisions online at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of Arizona Ethics Rules cited as basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arizona Supreme Court disbarred Respondent based on uncontested evidence that his conduct violated Arizona Ethics Rules: ER 1.2 (Scope of Representation and Allocation of Authority Between Client and Lawyer); ER 1.3 (Diligence); ER 1.4 (Communication); ER 1.15 (Safekeeping Property); ER 1.16(d) (Declining or Terminating Representation); and ER 8.1(b) (Bar Admission and Disciplinary Matters) by failing to disclose a necessary fact in a disciplinary matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These state ethics rule violations are adopted as the factual/reason basis for reciprocal discipline by the USPTO; when a state court finds violations of comparable ethical rules, the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline under § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service method and proof of service (certified mail and delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt number cited) and was delivered to Respondent on a specific date, which starts procedural timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document certified-mail receipt and delivery date to establish the start of the response period and the validity of the notice.
